transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. Um, I hope I'm giving you the right information here, but... I guess what made me come in is that, well, for the past year or so, I’ve been having a little trouble staying on track. 

It’s probably not a huge deal, honestly, but just the smallest things will pull me off what I’m doing before I can stop it. Like... a phone buzz, or somebody walking past my office, or even just a random thought popping up about my in-laws. I just sort of lose my place. I mean, I'm sure everyone gets a little sidetracked sometimes, right? Does that make sense as a reason to be here?
When did you first notice these difficulties with staying focused? Were they something you experienced even as a child, or did they start more recently in adulthood?

Um, well... I guess if I really look back on it... and I hope this is the kind of background you're looking for... but yeah, it was around when I was a kid, too. 

I mean, I was just a really energetic kid, you know? I definitely wasn't trying to be a troublemaker or anything. But, um, my teachers were always moving my seat around. I guess I just liked to chat a little too much with whoever was next to me, or sometimes I'd get up without asking just because I felt like I needed to stretch my legs. And, well, I'd sort of blurt things out before they even finished asking a question. Just because I was eager to participate, I think! 

Is that the kind of thing you mean? I really hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a terrible kid... I just had a lot of energy back then.
Can you tell me if these issues with staying focused or being easily distracted have continued into your adult life, or if they mostly stayed in the background after childhood?

Well, um... as an adult, I've honestly managed pretty well for the most part. I've worked really hard to build my career and keep things running smoothly, you know, so it really hasn't been a huge problem most of the time. 

But... I guess if I'm being completely honest—and I hope it's okay to bring up personal family stuff here—it's just been noticeably harder to manage lately. For about a year and two months, specifically. We've had this... well, a bit of a conflict with my in-laws, and it's just started taking over a lot of our family life. 

I really try my best not to let personal things affect my day-to-day focus, but with all that extra stress in the background, it's just been a little tougher to keep myself from getting sidetracked. Is it normal for family stress to make things like this flare up? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right context for why it's bothering me now.
Have you noticed any ongoing tendencies in adulthood, such as feeling restless, having trouble relaxing, or acting on impulse without thinking things through?

Um, well, I wouldn't say I'm impulsive or anything like that. I always try to be really thoughtful about my decisions, especially at work. But, um... I guess maybe the restless part? A little bit? 

I hope this doesn't sound disrespectful, because I really do value family time and my community, but... sometimes when I'm supposed to just sit still for a while, like at a long family dinner or during the volunteer meetings I help run at church, it just gets a little... tricky for me. It's not that I don't want to be there! It's just... I get this feeling, almost like there's a little motor running inside me? And I just feel this urge to move around, or at least be doing something with my hands, like tapping or adjusting things on the table. 

I try really hard to hide it so I don't bother anyone, but it's just a bit uncomfortable to just sit perfectly still. Is that the kind of restlessness you mean? I hope that doesn't make me sound impatient or rude to my family... I really do try my best to be present.
Do you find yourself feeling restless or needing to move around even in situations outside of family gatherings or meetings, like when you're at work or trying to relax at home?

Um, yeah... I guess it does happen at home, too. I really try to be good about relaxing, especially for my wife's sake, because I know she likes to unwind after a long day. I mean, I'm a good husband, I really try to be. But... well, if we're just trying to sit quietly together at night, or if I try to do that meditation stuff people say is so good for you... it's just really hard. 

I don't know, the quiet just sort of... gets under my skin a little bit? I hope that doesn't sound weird. It's just that I'll end up getting up to clear the dishes, or I'll start checking my phone, or I'll just start making comments about things. I'm not trying to ruin the mood or anything! I just... I like to be helpful, you know? Keeping busy. Is it okay that I struggle with the quiet like that? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way.
Do you also feel restless or have trouble staying still in other situations, like when you're at work, in a meeting, or even when you're alone at home?

Um, well... at work, I guess it does happen a little bit there too. I mean, I'm the CEO, so I'm in a lot of meetings, and I always try to be super attentive and respectful of my team's time. But, um... I guess I do have a habit of... well, bouncing my knee, or maybe clicking a pen? 

I really don't mean anything by it! It's just a way to channel that little bit of extra energy so I can focus better on what they're saying. But... I think maybe I've been shifting around in my chair a bit too much lately, because I've noticed people giving me these... looks. Like they think I'm trying to rush them along, or like I'm not listening. And I *am* listening, I promise! I hate the idea that I might be making my team feel rushed or unappreciated. 

I try to keep it under control, but it just sort of happens without me realizing it sometimes. Is it... is it normal for people to misinterpret things like that? I just hope I'm not being a bad leader by doing it. Does that make sense?
When you're not feeling stressed by family issues or other outside pressures, do you still find it hard to focus, or does your ability to concentrate improve significantly?

Um, well... I really try my best to stay completely focused, you know? I want to be a good listener and a good boss. I think I do a pretty good job most of the time! But... I guess, even on a good day, when things are totally calm... it can still be a little tough to keep my attention perfectly steady. 

Like, I can sit down with one of my managers, or start reading over a new planning document, and for the first few minutes, I am just totally locked in. But then... I don't know, it's almost like my brain just sort of slips a gear? And suddenly I realize I missed half of what they just said to me. 

I always feel terrible about it. I have to ask them to run it back, and I try to make a joke out of it so they don't think I'm ignoring them, but... I hate feeling like I'm wasting their time. I really do want to hear every word, I just... my focus sort of drifts off, even when I'm not stressed. Is that... is that the kind of thing you're asking about? I hope I'm explaining it right.
As a child, did you often run about or climb in situations where it was not appropriate, or have trouble playing quietly?

Um, yeah, I guess looking back... it was kind of like that when I was a kid, too. I mean, I was a good kid! I really tried to be good and listen to the teachers. I always wanted them to like me. But... well, they were always moving my seat around in class. 

I think I just had a lot of enthusiasm, you know? Like, I'd get so excited about a topic that I'd just sort of... blurt things out before they even finished asking the question. Or I'd talk a little too much to the kids next to me, just trying to be friendly. And sometimes I'd get up without asking, but it was usually just to throw something away or sharpen a pencil—I wasn't trying to be rebellious or anything! 

It's just... sitting still and being totally quiet for that long was really hard for me. I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a bad student. I really did try my best to follow the rules. Is it pretty common for kids to struggle with that kind of stuff? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
